name: Judith Butler
shortBio: American philosopher and gender theorist whose theory of gender performativity transformed feminist philosophy, queer theory, social ontology, and theories of precariousness and political assembly.
centralQuestion: How do reiterated social norms and discursive practices materialize sexed and gendered subjects rather than merely expressing a pre-given inner essence?

keyWorks.title: Gender Trouble: Feminism and the Subversion of Identity
keyWorks.description: Landmark text introducing gender performativity—arguing that gender is an effect of stylized repetition of acts regulated by normative power.

keyWorks.title: Bodies That Matter: On the Discursive Limits of 'Sex'
keyWorks.description: Clarifies materialization and citationality in response to constructivist critiques, bridging Foucault, Derrida, and psychoanalysis.

keyWorks.title: Precarious Life: The Powers of Mourning and Violence
keyWorks.description: Develops a social ethics of grievability and shared bodily vulnerability rooted in Levinasian responsibility.
